summary: Miconazole is an imidazole antifungal used topically for dermatophyte infections (athlete's foot, jock itch, ringworm) and cutaneous candidiasis, intravaginally for vulvovaginal candidiasis, and as an oromucosal gel/buccal tablet for oral candidiasis. Systemic absorption is low, so adverse effects are mainly local, but the oromucosal form can potentiate warfarin and other CYP-metabolized drugs.
indications: Tinea pedis (athlete's foot), tinea cruris (jock itch) and tinea corporis (ringworm)
Oropharyngeal candidiasis (oromucosal gel or buccal tablet)
Relief of associated itching, scaling, burning and irritation

moa: Miconazole inhibits the fungal cytochrome P450 enzyme 14-alpha-demethylase, blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. Depletion of ergosterol and accumulation of toxic sterol precursors disrupt the fungal cell membrane, increasing permeability and inhibiting fungal growth. It is active against dermatophytes and Candida species.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to miconazole or other imidazole antifungals or excipients
relative: Use of latex condoms/diaphragms with vaginal oil-based products (may weaken latex)
Oromucosal gel in infants under 4 months (choking risk)
monitor: Concurrent oral sulfonylureas or phenytoin (oral gel)

preg: Topical and short-course vaginal use is generally considered acceptable; systemic absorption is minimal. In the first trimester use intravaginal therapy only when clearly needed and as advised by a clinician.
lact: Compatible with breastfeeding for topical and vaginal use due to negligible systemic absorption. Avoid applying topical product directly to the nipple/areola when nursing.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required for topical or vaginal use given minimal systemic absorption.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required for topical or vaginal use. The oromucosal form has some systemic absorption; use with caution in significant hepatic disease.

major: Warfarin / coumarin anticoagulants (with oromucosal gel) - inhibition of CYP2C9 raises INR and bleeding risk; monitor INR
Sulfonylureas (with oral gel) - increased hypoglycemia risk
moderate: Statins metabolized by CYP3A4 (oral gel) - myopathy risk
Cisapride, pimozide, ergot alkaloids (oral gel) - increased toxicity
minor: Other topical agents on the same site - dilution/irritation
interactions.food: Apply oromucosal gel after food and hold in the mouth; no relevant food interaction for topical/vaginal use.
interactions.alcohol: No interaction with topical or vaginal use.
interactions.diagnostics: No significant laboratory interference with topical use; monitor INR with oromucosal use.

rare: Raised INR and bleeding with concomitant warfarin (oral gel)

missed: Apply the missed topical/vaginal/oral dose as soon as you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it. Do not apply a double amount.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with topical or vaginal use. Accidental ingestion of large amounts may cause GI upset; treat supportively. Excessive oral gel could intensify drug interactions (e.g., bleeding with warfarin); manage symptomatically.
